Professional Bra Size Calculator — Pro US / UK / EU / AU Sizing Tool for Fitters & Lingerie Pros

Use the bra size calculator below to find your exact bra size in US, UK, EU and AU sizing. All you need is a soft measuring tape and two measurements: your band (snug, under the bust) and your bust (loose, at the fullest part). The calculator returns both your standard size and your sister sizes , which can help you find a better fit when your usual size is out of stock.

Our calculator uses the standard underbust-and-bust method taught by lingerie fitters worldwide, then converts the result to whichever regional system you select. It is private — nothing leaves your browser — and the page works on every device.

How a Professional Bra Size Is Calculated

A bra size has two parts: a band number (the underbust, in inches or cm) and a cup letter (the difference between the bust and the band). The procedure is the same in every region:

  1. Measure your band. Wrap the tape snugly around your ribcage, directly under your breasts. The number in inches (rounded to the nearest even number) is your US/UK band size.
  2. Measure your bust. Wrap the tape loosely around the fullest part of your breasts, keeping it level. Round to the nearest inch.
  3. Compute your cup. Subtract the band from the bust. Each inch of difference is one cup letter: 1" = A, 2" = B, 3" = C, 4" = D, and so on.

The calculator handles the rounding and the regional conversion. For a deeper walkthrough, see our bra size guide or the how-to-measure article .

US vs UK vs EU vs AU Sizing

Most regions share the same band and cup letters up to cup D, then diverge. The key change happens at DD and beyond :

US UK EU AU Difference (in)
A A A A 1
B B B B 2
C C C C 3
D D D D 4
DD / E DD E DD 5
DDD / F E F E 6
G F G F 7
H FF H FF 8

So a US 34DDD is a UK 36E, an EU 75F and an AU 10E. Always check the brand's size chart before ordering internationally. For a complete comparison, see our US vs UK bra sizes guide .

What Are Sister Sizes?

Sister sizes are sizes that have the same cup volume but different band lengths. Going down a band means going up a cup letter, and vice versa. For example, a 36C and a 34D have approximately the same cup volume; the 34 band is just shorter.

Sister sizes are useful when:

  • Your usual size is out of stock.
  • You are between two band sizes.
  • One band's straps or band cuts in but a smaller band is too tight.

For a full explanation, see our sister sizes guide .

How to Measure Band Size

Stand in front of a mirror with a soft measuring tape. Wrap it around your ribcage, directly underneath the breast fold. Pull it snug — the way a bra band should feel — and round to the nearest whole inch. If you land on an odd number (e.g., 33), round down for a snugger fit or up for a more relaxed one. Most people should round to the nearest even number to match standard band sizing.

How to Measure Cup Size

Measure around the fullest part of your bust, keeping the tape level all the way around. The tape should sit loosely on the skin — don't compress the breast tissue. Round to the nearest whole inch. The difference between this number and your band is your cup size in the table above.

How Accurate Is This Calculator?

For most adults, the calculator gives the same result as a professional fitter within ±1 band size and ±1 cup letter. The remaining variability comes from breast shape, posture, and how the tape is held. If you are between sizes or have a non-standard shape (asymmetric, shallow, projected), the calculator will still give you a starting point, but a professional fitting or trying on several sizes is recommended.

Frequently Asked Questions

How accurate is the bra size calculator?

Within ±1 band and ±1 cup letter for most adults. It uses the same underbust-and-bust method as a professional fitter.

How do I figure out my bra size at home?

Measure snug under the bust for the band, and loosely around the fullest part for the bust. Subtract band from bust — each inch of difference is one cup letter. Use the calculator above to do the math and convert to US, UK, EU or AU.

What's a sister size?

A sister size has the same cup volume but a different band length. 36C and 34D are sister sizes. They are useful when your usual size is out of stock or you sit between band sizes.

How often should I re-measure?

Every 6–12 months, or after any significant weight change, pregnancy, or surgery. The body changes more than most people expect.

US vs UK — what changes after D?

After D, the US system uses DD, DDD, G, H… while the UK uses DD, E, F, FF, G… So a US 34DDD is a UK 36E. The calculator handles the conversion automatically.

Methodology & Editorial Review

This calculator implements the underbust-and-bust method (also called the band-and-bust or +0 method ), with band rounding to the nearest even number and cup letters assigned by 1-inch steps. Sizing theory is documented in our sister sizes article and on our bra size guide hub .
